messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: hosted-inference queue spike detected — total queued requests = 42,300 (all pools). p95 latency > 7.2s, error-rate (5m) = 8%. Autoscaler attempted scale but returned failures (quota/IC). Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/hosted-queue-spike

maya: I'm oncall, ack. Starting triage.

ops-bot: Runbook reference: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/hosted-queue-spike — follow section 'autoscaler-failure' and 'fallback-routing'. Logged incident id INC-2026-1799.

alex: Can someone confirm which pools are hot? Is this isolated to us-west?

jia: yes — hosted-prod-us-west primary. hosted-prod-us-west-gpu-pool at 98% utilization. Telemetry: queue growth from 6k -> 42k in ~12m. Autoscaler logs show repeated launch failures:
```
ERROR autoscaler: LaunchAttempt failed: InsufficientInstanceCapacity
ERROR autoscaler: AWS API RateLimitExceeded when Requesting 24 GPUs
ERROR autoscaler: QuotaExceeded: Requested 40 GPUs, but quota is 32
```

luke: From infra view: two things happening simultaneously — AWS AZ capacity pressure (InsufficientInstanceCapacity) and we've hit a per-account GPU quota ceiling. Autoscaler retries are causing backoff loops and queue amplification.

sophie: CS: multiple customers reporting errors — top impacted: acme-inc, widgetlabs, smartform. 7 clients with sustained 429s.

maya: Mitigations I'm initiating now (live):
- enable model-fallback route to smaller/quantized variants for non-critical keys (reduces GPU mem/latency)
- reduce frontend per-request concurrency for heavy API keys (MAX_CONCURRENCY 4 -> 2)
- pause batch-aggregation to cut tail latency
- open emergency request for preemptible GPU pool

alex: Commands to run?

maya: Executing:
```
infractl route set-fallback --selector "env:hosted" --model "redwood-small-quant" --priority 10
kubectl -n infra patch configmap autoscaler-config --type merge -p '{"data": {"max_gpus":"200"}}'  # temporary
```
Applied @ 1799123583. Expect autoscaler config to propagate ~60-120s.

ops-bot: Action recorded: fallback routing enabled; autoscaler-config patch submitted.

jia: After fallback enabled queue down to ~28k in 6m but still high p95 ~3.8s. ~6k requests still timing out per 5m window.

luke: Attempted scale-up returned AWS RunInstances 429/RequestLimitExceeded and a quota error. Opened cloud ticket CLD-893 (escalated to provider) and internal quota request QTA-412. Provider suggests alternate region provisioning.

sophie: Posting customer status: "Degraded performance for hosted inference (US-WEST). Temporary fallbacks and throttles active. Working on recovery; ETA 45-90 mins." :loudspeaker:

alex: Recommend soft-throttling largest API keys temporarily to reduce queue growth. Any objections?

jia: Implementing soft-limits now for top noisy keys (acme-inc, widgetlabs). Example:
```
curl -s -X POST https://admin.internal/ratelimit -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"key":"acme-inc","limit_rps":2}'
```
Applied at 1799123840.

maya: Also rolling an emergency route that will send 20% of traffic to us-east warm pool if provisioned. Preparing switch but will coordinate with luke.

luke: Cloud team replied: can provision GPUs in us-east but need cross-region routing + warm-up ~12m. Kicking preemptible warm pool build (estimated 12m). Creating resource pool: `hosted-warm-us-east-preempt` (ticket CLD-893-PR1).

ops-bot: Warm pool creation started. ETA ~12m.

jia: Metrics update: queue now ~12k after throttles + fallback + partial routing. Error rate down to 2.1%. p95 ~2.6s.

sophie: CS updated top customers and set up a special Slack channel for impacted tenant comms.

maya: Preparing structured handoff in ~25m. Current status: mitigations active (fallback routing, throttles to heavy keys, warm-pool request in progress). Customer impact: degraded perf and lower-quality responses for fallbacked traffic. Known risks: fallback may increase semantic regressions for a subset of evals; monitor QA channel.

alex: I'll take oncall after handoff. My priorities on shift: 1) ensure warm pool comes online and routes correctly, 2) monitor error rates and roll back fallback if errors >4% or CS reports major regressions, 3) continue cloud quota escalation.

luke: I'll stay on cloud escalation and coordinate cross-region provisioning. If provider can't supply capacity we'll provision more preemptible instances and reroute.

ops-bot: Incident updated — status: mitigation-in-progress | severity: high | owner: maya | handoff: alex @ 1799124920 UTC | incident-id: INC-2026-1799

maya: Handoff notes -> checklist:
- confirm warm pool `hosted-warm-us-east-preempt` becomes healthy and traffic split applies
- keep fallback routing active until queue < 2k for 10m
- monitor top-customer error telemetry and escalate to CS for direct outreach if errors persist
- rollback plan: revert `route set-fallback` and restore batching if error-rate < 0.5% and p95 < 500ms for 10m

alex: Taking the handoff. Links: Grafana dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/hosted/queue | Autoscaler logs: https://logs.redwood/autoscaler?from=1799123400&to=1799125000 | Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/hosted-queue-spike

sophie: I'll continue external comms and monitor customer replies.

incident-bot: FINAL: handoff completed to alex at 1799124920 — incident remains open, mitigation in progress.
